description:
FILED s473t2 (Opus triage of the 152 causeless blessed sweep rows), on main 0d783d24.
Probes scratch/s473t2/probes/p11-misc.pl D/E and p6-multideref.pl A/B.

ROWS BEHIND IT: perl-tests/array.t 109, 111, 112, 114 (Bug #37350, blessed as the
one collapsed unnamed key `array.t 127` -- unnamed rows share a key, #1041) and
perl-tests/multideref.t 1 ("strict refs") and 3 ("no strict refs, exist")
= 6 rows.

PROBE (a) -- a NUMERIC symbolic array name (array.t, Bug #37350):
    no strict 'refs'; our @array = (1..4);
    $#{@array} = 7;                 # @array in scalar context is 4 -> the array @4
    print "D: [", $#{4}, "]";       # perl 7, PCL -1
    push @{@array}, 23;
    print "E: [", $4[8] // 'UNDEF', "]";   # perl 23, PCL UNDEF

PROBE (b) -- a symbolic HASH deref inside an element chain (multideref.t):
    package strict_refs; our %foo; my @a = ('foo');
    eval { use strict 'refs'; $a[0]{k} = 7 };  # perl DIES "Can't use string"
    no strict 'refs'; $a[0]{k} = 13;           # perl: $strict_refs::foo{k} = 13
  perl: died / 13        PCL: NO-DIE / undef
So the write went to a detached anonymous hash: neither the strict-refs refusal
nor the symbolic resolution happens when the string sits in an element slot.

Both halves are the same missing step: when a dereference's operand is a plain
string (or a number), it names a package variable, and `strict refs` decides
whether that is legal.  PCL treats such an operand as an autovivified anonymous
container.

=== DONE (s473b) ===
CLOSED s473b (Opus, 2026-09-07) inside commit dde02df9 (#1241's read-path
vivification), because the two are one mechanism: an intermediate slot holding
a DEFINED non-reference was CLOBBERED by the vivification â `$h{a}="zz";
$h{a}{b}=1` replaced the string with a fresh hash, where perl writes `$zz{b}`
(a symbolic reference).  That was neither of perl's two answers, and once the
READ path vivified too it would have become silent DATA LOSS on a read.  The
four `p-autoviv-*` accessors now route a defined slot through
`p-ensure-hashref` / `p-ensure-arrayref` â the same pair `$ref->{k}` has always
used, so the twins cannot disagree again.
subject: BUG: a SYMBOLIC array/`$#{}` dereference whose name is not a plain identifier does not reach the package array -- `$#{@array} = 7; $#{4}` reads -1, `@{4}` never grows, and `$a[0]{k}` on a string neither dies under `strict refs` nor resolves without it
